title: Labour protests in Bangladesh garment sector threaten export deadlines
content:
Bangladesh’s garment shippers face missed sailings and mounting pressure on delivery schedules as labour protests halt production and disrupt cargo movements to Chittagong port.
Production was suspended at around 690 garment factories today, according to the latest information from Bangladesh, while roadblocks hampered the movement of export cargo from Dhaka factories to the port.
The disruption threatens shipment schedules on two fronts: factories may struggle to complete orders

title: Poor new year liner schedule reliability only improves as summer arrives
content:
Global schedule reliability has become more seasonal, while weekly liner service deployments have grown increasingly volatile since the pandemic, according to new analysis by Sea-Intelligence.
Drawing on its Global Liner Performance database, which tracks monthly vessel arrivals from July 2011 to September 2026, the consultant found a stronger relationship between declining punctuality and the severity of delays, at , alongside more pronounced seasonal fluctuations in reliability.

title: SLOSCO – Sierra Leone’s latest Chinese shipping venture
content:
After two ambitious Chinese-backed infrastructure projects were abandoned or stalled, Sierra Leone is turning to another Chinese partner to develop a “national” shipping industry. The financing model has changed, but familiar questions remain.
On 19 October, Sierra Leone inaugurated its new national shipping company, Sierra Leone Ocean Shipping Company (SLOSCO), with ambitions to operate, in time, 50 vessels and capture a significant share of the country’s maritime trade.
